situation:
You are to assume the role of marketing manager at STREET LANTERN TRUCKS, a food truck fleet operator running six trucks in a tourist city. The founder (judge) has asked to meet with you about what the company should do with the attention the fleet has suddenly received.

STREET LANTERN TRUCKS opened two years ago, and its cooks press each flatbread by hand at the truck window while the guest watches. A visitor's video of that window, posted last month, has been viewed more than two million times. Lines now run forty minutes at the two trucks parked near the convention center, and many visitors leave before they order.

Pressing the flatbreads at a central commissary and storing them frozen until each truck's morning run would double the guests a truck serves in an hour and let the fleet add stops in the hotel and convention districts. It would also require leasing freezer space, and it would take the hand-pressing at the truck window out of the guest's view.

Keeping the pressing at the truck window would protect what the video showed and what the visitors came for, at the cost of the forty-minute lines, the visitors who leave before they order, and the stops the fleet cannot add before its first round of funding runs out this winter. The investors who put in that round want the fleet growing.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation, a plan for reaching the visitor market the video has drawn, and a positioning concept for a new griddle bowl the trucks would add. The founder (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the founder's (judge's) questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
